event: Nala pockets the seed stone and goes after the wolf, her braid ready.
The prints end at the water's edge. She works the banks downstream first. The mud lies smooth.
Upstream the brook runs over stony shallows, bare wet stone from bank to bank.
She keeps on, eyes on both banks, the charcoal smoke growing ahead.
Half a mile up the trees open on a clearing. A low hut smokes beside a charcoal mound.
On the south bank's shingle she finds wet claw scrapes, leading up out of the water.
Black-matted fur is caught on a bramble. It stinks of rot.
The scrapes lead past the mound, toward a brush lean-to behind the hut.
The hut door creaks open. A stooped old woman in a gray shawl steps out, soot on her hands.
"Lost, love?" Her voice is soft and kind. "There's nettle tea on, if you're cold."
Nala's sight shows her more. Around the old woman hangs an aura of sick violet-black.
